(None of that is issue kit. Not one piece. I have made a targeting error.)
(Bare hands. No insignia. I have been pointed at the wrong throat.)
(A door stood open for one heartbeat, and someone was standing in it. Not who I was told.)
(There. In the glass. For one moment the reflection was a boy, and the armour was the lie.)
(I know what it looks like when something is wearing a shadow that is not its own.)
(Hold on. That's a girl in a hospital shirt. Who am I FIGHTING?)
(No crest. No colours. I have struck someone who never swore to anything.)
(The cut was true. The target was false. That is on my hand, not hers.)
(So light. There is hardly anything to him. All that weight was painted on.)
(Stop. Go back. One second ago - that was a face. That was a real face.)
(That ain't a house dealer. That's another mark, same as me. We've both been played.)
(Rags, and a coat of frost. No armour. Nothing for me to take hold of. There never was.)
Then the veil closes over the face again, seamless, and it is only an agent, getting to its feet.
The Crater floor splits with light. A rift, opening straight up - through the cloud, toward the Spire. The agent looks at it. Looks at you. And runs for the light.
(Gone. Straight up. ...I saw a face. I am SURE I saw a face.)
You are down on the glass, and your arms will not lift you. The agent stands over you. Its weapon comes up.
It stays up. For one heartbeat the white armour shivers like heat over a road - and whoever is under it is breathing as hard as you are.
(Halcyon doesn't hesitate. I've SEEN them not hesitate. ...Why is it hesitating?)
(The orderlies never paused. Not once. ...Why does this one pause?)
(A hunter that will not finish the kill is not hunting. It was driven here. Like me.)
(Its hand is shaking. Their machines do not shake.)
(It could end this. It does not want to. ...Neither did I.)
(Go on, then. ...It's not going to. Lab staff ALWAYS finish the procedure.)
(It's looking at me like it has just seen something. What did it see?)
(It will not strike a banked fire. Then it is not one of theirs. Theirs would.)
(Clean shot. Zero range. Not taking it. That is NOT in the Halcyon manual.)
(I would not have waited. Whoever that is, they are kinder than I am. Or less sure.)
(The door is open and it will not walk through. I know that look. It is afraid of the next room.)
(In the glass under me, the thing standing over me has no armour on at all.)
(It had the light in its hand, and did not put it out. I will remember that.)
(Beat me fair. And now it's just standing there, looking sorry. Suits don't look sorry.)
(It holds the stroke. That is mercy. Halcyon has never once shown me mercy.)
(It will not cut a fallen opponent. Whoever trained that hand was no soldier.)
(The weight has gone out of it, all at once. As if it had set something down.)
(This is the one ending I never saw. It does not strike. Why did I never see that?)
(Winning hand, and it won't lay it down. Nobody the house hired plays like that.)
(It won. It's got me. And it's the one that's shaking.)
The Crater floor splits with light. A rift, opening straight up toward the Spire. The agent lowers its weapon, looks at you a moment longer - and runs for the light.
(Up. It went UP. ...Get up. Whoever that was - get UP.)
THE CRATER RIFT. A tear of light from the glass at your feet to the underside of Aurelia - and through it, to the Halcyon Spire.
(Everything that goes UP pays somebody. Not this time. This one I'm taking for free.)
(I fell out of that city. I am going back in by the front door.)
Whoever was under that white armour went up ahead of you. You mean to find out who.

The grass, and the thunderheads, and an old woman at the standing stones who says: "There you are, storm-boy."
The frozen harbour in spring, the ice breaking up, and a choir on a ship that finally lets go of the note.
The steppe, the herd, and a wolf made of stormlight running to meet you across the grass.
The high eyrie over the harbour, and a white falcon folding out of the sky onto your glove.
The ring of standing stones, humming, and the children following your shadow again.
The blue forge, still burning, and the old smith calling you in from the cold.
The ridge where the wind never stops, and your little sister shouting your name from below.
The deep vents under the harbour, red and warm and patient, waiting for the ember-carrier.
The storm-season festival, and the whole sky going gold because you lit the fuse.
The sea wall at dusk, one lamp after another coming alight, and nobody seeing who lit them.
A tent with two flaps, and your mother at the far one, counting to ten, and you coming out of the right one.
The harbour ice at noon, and the girl underneath it, smiling up at you.
The harbour at night, with nothing in the dark that is not supposed to be there. You keep it that way.
Festival day, a hundred kites, and one still tangled in the only tree for a mile. You reach.
The harbour gate, and forty shadows of a company that stands down at last.
An old school, a teacher, a square of white paper, and one line of ink.
A sky full of stars that fall only when you let them.
The tide table on the harbour wall, and you, for once, exactly on time.
A card table in a storm, and your grandmother, laughing, dealing you in.
A smithy, and every tool on the wall turning to see who has come home.
A wagon in the rain, a thousand and one paper cranes, and your father laughing until he has to sit down.
The far camp at the end of the steppe. They do not ask for the message. They ask your name, and you tell them.
The harbour at the turn of the tide, and a sick child, and the fever going out with the water.
The sea wall at night, and a ship far out in the ice, steering home by the light you lit.
A long-house under the snow, and the children shouting your short name, not because they are afraid.
It is done. I built it to save one city, and it nearly ate three. Thank you for letting me be the one to switch it off.
Aurelia is coming down. Slowly, the engineers say. A year. I think we will all be better for being closer to the ground.
The Engine core. A wheel of violet light as tall as a house, turning slowly over the floor. In front of it, a man in black stands with his hands behind his back.
Calder Sayle. Director of Halcyon. I have been waiting for the two of you for a year. Apart, as I arranged it. And yet here you are.
You came through the first pulse at its two ends. Together you could turn it back. Apart, you were only fuel. I hung the veil so you would never stand in the same room.
Then I will finish it myself. The second pulse welds the three worlds into one, and Aurelia never falls. Stand aside, or be part of it.
The Director staggers back - into the light of the Engine. It does not throw him out. It takes him in.
Yes. YES. A year in the core, and I never once dared to step INTO it. ...I should have.
What comes out of the light is no longer a man.
The fused thing breaks apart, and from the middle of it a single figure rises, white as the inside of a star: THE CONVERGENCE.
Not alone. Not this time. I am here.
Room for one more? I'm not missing this.
Together, then.
Your partner fights beside you, and presses two healing items into your hand (Q). Everything you have lost in two worlds is in your hands at once: your ULTIMATE is ready. Hold W and press I.
The Convergence comes apart into light. The Engine shudders, and slows, and for the first time in a year it is quiet.
The key. Kessen said it runs backwards once. Only once.
The key! Backwards, once. Kessen said once. Don't drop it.
You put the core key into the Engine, together, and turn it the other way.
Everything goes white. And then, one at a time, like lamps along a sea wall, the memories come home.
I can hear the harbour. ...I will see you again. I have decided. Two worlds is not so far.
I can smell the grass. ...See you around, yeah? Two worlds isn't that far. I'll walk it.
Count on it.
I will be there.
